versions.changelog: This release fixes two security problems that affect any server where more than one person uses Jellyscribe, so please update. First, the admin dashboard showed account names, film titles and error messages as raw page content, so a user could save a specially crafted account name that ran code in an admin's browser the next time they opened the dashboard. Every value is now shown as plain text, and an old, unused stats page with the same problem has been removed. Second, Jellyscribe remembered Letterboxd and Serializd logins by account name alone, so a user who entered someone else's Letterboxd username or Serializd email with any password could end up syncing, reviewing and rating as that person. A remembered login is now only reused when the password matches too. Households that deliberately share one Letterboxd or Serializd account across several Jellyfin users are unaffected. Both problems were found and fixed by Wouter Stulp. Thank you, Wouter.

Many anime are split into several seasons in Jellyfin but listed on Serializd as one long season. The Apothecary Diaries is a good example: Jellyfin shows a season 1 and a season 2, while Serializd, which follows TMDb, has one long season covering both. Watching season 2 in Jellyfin produced nothing on Serializd, because Jellyscribe asked for a season 2 that Serializd does not have and skipped the episode. Jellyscribe now recognises that shape and logs the episode to season 1 at its running number, so season 2 episode 1 lands on Serializd as episode 25. It only does this for shows Serializd keeps as a single season, and only when it knows exactly how many episodes the earlier seasons have, so a show Serializd simply has not added a new season for yet is still skipped rather than logged to the wrong episode.

If you renamed a Jellyfin user, their Jellyscribe dashboard suddenly showed zero films, zero episodes and no recent activity, as if nothing had ever been synced. Nothing was lost: every entry was still there, but each one was filed under the name the user had when it was written, and the dashboard only looked for the new name. The same mix-up quietly weakened the duplicate checks, so a film synced before the rename could be logged to Letterboxd a second time afterwards. History is now tied to the Jellyfin user itself rather than to their name, and existing entries are linked up automatically the first time this version starts. The one case this cannot repair on its own is a user who was already renamed before updating: their older entries stay filed under the old name.

Clicking Jellyscribe used to reload the whole Jellyfin web app and drop you onto a plugin settings page. It now opens as a proper page inside Jellyfin, the way Jellyfin Enhanced's Bookmarks does: no reload, Jellyfin's header and menu stay put, and the back button takes you straight back to where you were. You can also bookmark it, since it has its own address ending in #/jellyscribe. On Jellyfin 12, where the sidebar was replaced by a menu under your profile picture, Jellyscribe now appears in that menu, so it is reachable there for the first time. Everything on the page works as before, and the old settings-page address still works.

The Jellyscribe link in Jellyfin's sidebar used to appear only if you had also installed the File Transformation plugin, so many people never saw it and had to dig through the dashboard to find their settings. Jellyscribe now adds the link itself, the same way Jellyfin Enhanced adds its own menu, and nothing on your server's disk is changed. If you already use File Transformation, nothing changes for you and you still get exactly one link. The link also now works on servers that run Jellyfin under a sub-path such as /jellyfin, where it used to point at the wrong address. On Jellyfin 12, the web client moved its menu into the profile button, so the link doesn't show there yet; open Jellyscribe from Dashboard, Plugins instead.

Until now the Verify login button only worked for Serializd. For a Letterboxd account it said the login would be checked on the first sync, so a wrong password or a mistyped name went unnoticed until something quietly failed to appear on Letterboxd. Verify login now works for Letterboxd too: it signs in the same way syncing will and tells you whether it got in, and if not, the reason Letterboxd gave. It also catches a common mix-up: Letterboxd no longer lets you sign in with your email address, so Jellyscribe now asks for your Letterboxd username instead and explains why if you enter an email.

Jellyscribe sends your rating along when it logs a film to your Letterboxd diary, and that happens the moment the credits roll. Most people rate afterwards, and until now those ratings never left Jellyfin: the film was already logged, so later syncs skipped it. Jellyscribe now notices when you change a film's rating and, about ten seconds after you settle on a score, sets it as your Letterboxd rating for that film. Jellyfin's own web app has no star rating, only favourites, so the usual way in is a review written with Jellyfin Enhanced 12.10 or later with its option to copy review stars into Jellyfin switched on; ratings from any other app that saves them to Jellyfin work too. Only real changes are sent: ratings already in Jellyfin when you update are left alone until you change them, and favouriting or rewatching a film leaves Letterboxd alone. If Letterboxd is briefly unreachable, the rating is retried a few times. As on Letterboxd itself, rating a film marks it watched and takes it off your watchlist. Clearing a rating in Jellyfin does not remove it from Letterboxd, and some apps, Infuse among them, keep ratings to themselves and never save them to Jellyfin, so those still cannot be synced. Each Letterboxd account has a new Sync ratings to Letterboxd switch, on by default.

Until now Jellyscribe sent every film and episode you finished to your linked accounts, whichever library it lived in. If you already track some of that somewhere else, anime on AniList for example, those watches were turning up on Letterboxd or Serializd as well, and the only way to stop it was to switch the whole account off. Each linked account now has an Excluded libraries list in its settings. Tick a library there and nothing from it is sent to that account, whether by the daily catch-up or the moment you finish watching. The setting is per account, so two people sharing a Jellyfin login can make different choices, and a library you leave unticked syncs exactly as before. Exclusion only applies from now on: anything already logged stays where it is, and diary import and watchlist sync still look at every library.

In Jellyfin's Scheduled Tasks page, most of Jellyscribe's tasks were still filed under a heading called Letterboxd, left over from before the plugin was renamed, while one sat under Jellyscribe. That even put the Serializd tasks for TV under Letterboxd. Every Jellyscribe task, film and TV alike, now appears together under Jellyscribe. Nothing about how or when the tasks run has changed.

If your Letterboxd watchlist or your list of watched films was longer than about a hundred titles, Jellyscribe only ever saw the first hundred. A watchlist of a thousand films turned into a playlist of ninety-nine, and the diary import only marked your first hundred watched films as played. The fix shipped in 2.4.0 for this did not hold: it asked Letterboxd for the next page in a way Letterboxd quietly ignores, so every request came back with the first page again and nothing warned that anything was missing. Jellyscribe now asks for each page exactly the way Letterboxd expects, so the whole list comes through, and if Letterboxd ever stops handing over new pages, the sync stops, says so in the log, and leaves your playlist exactly as it was instead of quietly shrinking it. Run a watchlist sync after updating and your playlist will fill in with everything that was missing.

If you run Ghostery, uBlock Origin with annoyance lists, AdGuard or Brave shields, the Raw cookies field in the account settings could simply not appear. The label was there, the box was not, and nothing showed up in the browser console to explain it. The cause was on our side: the field was named with the word "cookie" in it, and blockers carry sweeping rules that hide anything named that way in order to kill cookie consent banners. Ours got caught in the net. The field has been renamed internally so blockers leave it alone, and it still reads Raw cookies on screen. This mattered more than it sounds, because pasting cookies is exactly what we recommend when Cloudflare or two-factor authentication blocks a normal password login, so the people most in need of that box were the ones least likely to see it.

Importing your Serializd diary could fail outright with a confusing error about an element of type Number. The cause was that Serializd diaries contain reviews of whole seasons and whole shows, not just individual episodes, and those entries carry no episode number. Jellyscribe tried to read one anyway and the whole import stopped there, so nothing was imported at all. Those entries are not episode watches, so they are now simply skipped and the rest of the diary imports normally. If your Serializd import has been failing, it should work on the next run with no changes needed at your end.

Jellyfin 12 changed the way plugins add items to a playlist, and Jellyscribe was still asking the old way. The result was that on Jellyfin 12 your watchlist playlist silently stopped being filled in, while everything else carried on working normally. Jellyscribe now detects which version of that API the server offers and uses the right one, so a single release keeps working on Jellyfin 10.11 and Jellyfin 12 alike. If you are on Jellyfin 12 and your watchlist playlist has been sitting empty or stale, this release fixes it and the next watchlist sync will fill it in. Jellyfin 12 is now explicitly supported.

When a Letterboxd login fails three times in a row, Jellyscribe pauses that account and shows "Login failing, sync paused". Correcting the password was supposed to clear that and resume on the next run. It did if you edited the account from the user page, but not from the admin dashboard, because those two save through different paths and only one of them reset the pause. Admins were left stuck: the password was right, the badge still said failing, and even deleting the account and adding it again changed nothing, because the paused state is remembered per Letterboxd username and a new account simply inherited it. Saving an account from the dashboard now clears the pause whenever its password or cookies changed, so a corrected login is retried on the next sync.

Version 2.4.0 made sure new Seerr requests get approved so they actually reach Radarr and Sonarr. It did nothing for requests that were already sitting in Seerr waiting for approval, which for anyone who had been hit by the problem was most of them. The reason is that Jellyscribe skips any title Seerr already has a request for, so those requests were never looked at again and nothing ever approved them. Upgrading appeared to change nothing at all. Jellyscribe now checks for watchlist titles left waiting for approval and approves those too, so an existing backlog clears itself on the next watchlist sync instead of needing to be worked through by hand.

Two problems that quietly cut the watchlist feature off at the knees. Large watchlists only ever synced their first hundred films, because the plugin asked Letterboxd for the next page using the wrong field name and so always concluded there was nothing more to fetch. Everything past the first page simply never arrived. Separately, watchlist titles sent to Seerr were created but never downloaded: Seerr only hands a request to Radarr or Sonarr once it has been approved, and it decides that from the permissions of the person the request belongs to rather than the admin API key the plugin uses, so requests for anyone without auto-approve sat in the pending queue forever. Jellyscribe now approves the requests it creates, and a new switch in the Seerr settings turns that off if you would rather review them yourself.

Films and episodes that Jellyfin marks watched through real playback have always synced with the correct date. But checking a title watched by hand, using the checkmark rather than actually playing it, could leave Jellyfin's own watched-date field set to January 1st 1970 instead of a real date, and the plugin trusted that value as-is. The fix treats an epoch-adjacent watched date the same way it already treats a missing one: there's no real watch date to log yet, so the sync waits rather than posting a bogus entry to Letterboxd or Serializd. Once Jellyfin records an actual playback date for the title, it syncs normally.

When a Letterboxd password goes stale, the plugin no longer retries the login forever. After three consecutive failed logins, syncing for that account pauses itself: no more login attempts (protecting you from Letterboxd rate limiting), a warning appears in Jellyfin's activity log where admins actually look, and the account card in both dashboards shows a "login failing" badge with the date it started. Re-save the account's credentials and syncing resumes on the next run; watches from the paused period are picked up by the scheduled catch-up, so nothing is lost.

The review modal now shows the rating you already gave. Instead of always opening at "No rating", it looks up the rating stored in Jellyfin, whether you set it in the Jellyfin web UI, a client app like Infuse, or an earlier Jellyscribe review, and pre-fills the stars for you, for films, shows, and individual episodes. The star widget also supports half stars now: click the left half of a star for a .5 rating, matching what Letterboxd itself accepts, so a 7/10 in Jellyfin finally displays as the 3.5 stars it really is.

The sidebar link this plugin adds to Jellyfin's nav is injected by registering with the File Transformation plugin once, at Jellyfin startup. That registration was racing File Transformation's own startup init, so on some restarts (including scheduled ones) it silently failed and the link just never appeared, with nothing in the logs beyond a generic, undiagnosable error. Registration now retries a few times before giving up, and a real failure logs the actual cause instead of a useless wrapper message.

Watchlist auto-requests now show up in your sync history. If your watchlist syncs with "auto-request via Jellyseerr" turned on, a successful request used to only ever show up in the server log, there was no way to see it from the dashboard itself. Now every title your watchlist successfully requests (film or TV) gets its own entry in your sync history, with the real title, right alongside your regular Letterboxd and Serializd activity. A request that fails shows up too, so if Jellyseerr rejects something you can see exactly what and when instead of wondering why your watchlist "isn't working."

A few follow-ups to the 2.0.0 rebrand. The admin and user dashboard headers lost their "by Lachlan Young and AI" credit line during the redesign, it's back. The opt-in anonymous telemetry, which only ever counted Letterboxd film syncs, now counts Serializd TV syncs and errors too, since that pipeline was never touched when TV support was built. And the Logs tab's Refresh button, which had been dumping a raw JSON blob into the panel instead of readable log lines, now shows the actual logs.

Two things land together in this release. First, the plugin is renamed from "Letterboxd Sync" to Jellyscribe, a name and a look that actually cover both services it now talks to, instead of the old identity that borrowed Letterboxd's own name and brand colors. Nothing about the rename requires any action, your plugin auto-updates in place, every linked account, sync history entry, and setting carries over untouched, and the repository URL you already have configured does not change.

Second, the plugin no longer stops at films. Link a Serializd account on the new TV / Serializd tab and TV episodes sync to Serializd automatically, watched status in real time as you finish an episode, with a daily catch-up for anything missed and a Sync TV Now button to run it on demand, each entry dated to when you actually watched it rather than when the sync ran.

Star ratings and favorites mirror to Serializd's rating and like, and you can post a written review straight from the dashboard, at the show or episode level. Your Serializd watchlist syncs back into Jellyfin too, as a browsable collection and a playable episode queue, with an optional Jellyseerr auto-request for anything still missing from your library.

Films still go to Letterboxd exactly as before, the two are completely independent, so a Serializd hiccup never touches your Letterboxd sync. Each Jellyfin user links their own Serializd account (by email or username), and passwords are encrypted at rest the same way Letterboxd credentials are.

If the "Import Letterboxd diary as Jellyfin watched" task ran and did nothing, it used to finish in a second and leave no trace in the log, so a switched-off toggle looked identical to a broken feature. The task now says why it skipped each user (for example, an account exists but diary import is not turned on, with a pointer to the setting), reports when your Letterboxd returned no films, and always ends with a one-line summary of what it checked. A stuck progress banner on the dashboard for empty diaries is also fixed. If reverse sync has not been working for you, update, run the task once, and the log will now tell you exactly why.

**"Send logs to developer" now tells you when there is nothing to send.** Previously, if the plugin had not logged anything recently, the send dialog reported success but the bundle arrived empty, and neither you nor the developer could tell why. The dialog now warns you when no plugin log lines were found, with a hint to reproduce the problem first and send again, and every bundle includes a small status line saying which log files were read and how many lines matched, so support requests no longer dead-end on an empty bundle.
Docs-only; ships no release.

A small improvement to the opt-in anonymous telemetry: alongside the existing per-week sync bucket, the weekly ping now includes a lifetime sync bucket. Until now, an instance reporting zero syncs in a week was indistinguishable from one where syncing never worked at all; the lifetime bucket separates the two, so setup problems can be spotted and fixed. Same privacy rules as everything else: a coarse bucket only (0, 1-10, 11-100, 100+), never exact numbers, and nothing is sent unless you opted in.

Your Letterboxd password, session cookies, and Seerr API key are now encrypted before they are written to disk, instead of sitting in the plugin config file as plaintext. Nothing changes about how you use the plugin: existing saved credentials are picked up and upgraded automatically the next time they are saved, no re-entry needed.

No functional changes to syncing. The project now documents openly how it is built: a new AI.md page explains that most of the plugin is AI-written under human direction and review, what tooling is used, and the checks every change passes before it ships. The Code of Conduct is rewritten to something honest for a one-person project, and the README links to all of it.

A second repository entry for this plugin, an edge-cached mirror of the exact same manifest, is added to your Jellyfin catalog next to the existing GitHub one, a single time. Your GitHub entry is never touched, so updates keep working even if the mirror is unreachable, and if you would rather not have the mirror you can simply delete it: the plugin will not add it back. The mirror counts an anonymous, weekly-rotating hash per request so we can see roughly how many servers run the plugin; no IP addresses or personal data are ever stored, and this is entirely separate from the opt-in telemetry. The mirror also no longer caches upstream GitHub errors at the edge, so a brief GitHub hiccup cannot pin a failed response for other users.

No functional changes to syncing. This release adds an anonymous, privacy-preserving install counter so the developer can see roughly how many Jellyfin servers run the plugin. No personal data is collected: your IP address is never stored, and the anonymous weekly fingerprint used to avoid double-counting cannot be traced back to you or linked across weeks.

Fixes a sync failure introduced when Letterboxd changed their website. Films stopped logging to your diary because the plugin could no longer read each film's identifier from its Letterboxd page. The plugin now reads the new page format, so watched films sync again.
test: strip instance_id before payload raw-count assertions to fix random-GUID flake

Jellyseerr and Overseerr have merged into a single project called Seerr. The plugin now uses the new name everywhere you see it, in the settings page, your personal account page, and the documentation, so the labels match what you see in the app you are connecting to. Nothing about the integration changes: your existing Seerr URL, API key, and per-account settings are kept, and there is nothing to reconfigure.
No functional changes. CI now uploads JUnit test results to Codecov Test Analytics so flaky tests and failures are tracked across releases. Nothing in the plugin itself changes.

Letterboxd often blocks plain username/password login with a Cloudflare or reCAPTCHA challenge, and accounts with two-factor authentication can never log in that way at all. This release makes raw cookies the clearly recommended way to authenticate, warns you when you save an account without them, and turns the cryptic two-factor login failure into a message that tells you exactly what to do.

- Raw Cookies are now presented as the recommended way to authenticate, on both the admin settings page and your personal account page, with a short explanation of why password-only login is unreliable.
- Saving an enabled account that has a password but no raw cookies now shows a non-blocking warning, so you find out before the first sync fails. The save still goes through.
- Accounts with two-factor authentication enabled now fail login with a clear, actionable message instead of a vague generic error, telling you to add raw cookies (including cf_clearance) or disable 2FA.

**Send your logs to the developer in one click.** Reporting a problem with Letterboxd Sync used to mean digging through Jellyfin's log files and pasting the right lines into a GitHub issue. This release adds a **"Send logs to developer"** button to the Logs tab that does it for you.

**What it does**
- Click the button and the plugin bundles your recent Letterboxd Sync log lines (the same ones already shown on the Logs tab) and uploads them privately, then hands you a short **reference code** like `LBX-7Q2F9K`. Quote that code when you open a GitHub issue and the developer can pull your exact logs, no more copy-pasting walls of text.
- A confirmation step lets you **preview exactly what will be sent** (the real log lines and a telemetry snapshot, byte-for-byte what gets uploaded) and add a short note describing what went wrong.

**Privacy, stated plainly**
- Unlike the anonymous weekly telemetry from 1.16.0, **logs are not anonymous**: they can contain your Letterboxd username or film titles, and the bundle is linked to your install's telemetry ID. The dialog says this before you send, nothing leaves your server until you confirm, and passwords, cookies, and auth tokens are never logged.
- Works whether or not you have anonymous telemetry enabled. Uploaded bundles are stored privately and **auto-deleted after 90 days**.

**Also in this release**
- **Stronger log access control:** the plugin's log endpoint now requires administrator access. Previously any signed-in Jellyfin user could read the Letterboxd Sync logs (which name every linked Letterboxd account and watched film); on shared or family servers this is now admin-only.
- Better diagnostics when you do send logs: full multi-line error traces are captured intact (they were previously fragmented), log text is cleaned of stray terminal control codes, and the bundle always records your Jellyfin version.

Nothing changes unless you choose to use the new button.

New: anonymous, opt-in usage telemetry — off by default, enabled via a one-time dashboard banner or Settings. One small bucketed ping a week (versions, enabled features, size buckets; never film titles, usernames, IPs, or exact numbers), a Preview-exact-JSON button showing precisely what's sent, a regenerable random instance ID, and an extra capped ping when errors start occurring so fleet-wide breakage is caught early. Full payload documented in the README. No other behaviour changes.

Fixes the plugin failing to load (showing as disabled) on Jellyfin 10.11.9 and 10.11.10 for versions v1.14.1 through v1.15.3: those releases were compiled against a newer Jellyfin SDK than the advertised minimum. The plugin is now always compiled against the oldest supported Jellyfin SDK, a policy enforced by CI, so the advertised minimum version is the real one. If your plugin recently stopped working, update to this version and restart Jellyfin. No feature changes.

Adds the design spec for upcoming anonymous, opt-in usage telemetry (minimal bucketed payload, off by default, one-time prompt, full payload preview) and an automated regression canary. Spec only; no telemetry code or behaviour changes in this release.
Maintenance: fixes an intermittent CI-only test failure where a background sync spawned by one test could still hold the sync gate when the next test ran. No plugin behaviour changes.
Documentation: the Releases page on letterboxdsync.dev now has structured highlights for v1.13.4 through v1.15.0. No plugin behaviour changes.

New opt-in per-account setting "Also backfill requests for already-available watchlist films": creates attributed Jellyseerr requests for watchlist films that entered the library without one, so "who requested this?" is always answerable. Off by default; existing behavior unchanged.
build: Bump Jellyfin.Controller and Jellyfin.Model
fix(sync): skip films with no LastPlayedDate and abandon films after 3 consecutive failures
test: expand plugin coverage to 89.8% line / 81.4% branch

Maintenance release. Two preventative changes aimed at the next Jellyfin SDK ABI surprise. Dependabot now watches the `Jellyfin.Controller` and `Jellyfin.Model` packages and opens a PR the day a new patch ships, so any breaking ABI change is caught by CI on our timeline rather than via a user bug report (the v1.13.0 fix only existed because Jellyfin 10.11.9's silent removal of `IUserManager.Users` surfaced as bigrichwood's report). And the version-gate CI check now refuses a patch-only version bump when `targetAbi.txt` changes in the same PR, because moving the Jellyfin compatibility floor stops a cohort of users from being offered the next plugin update and that warrants at least a minor bump so the change shows up clearly in the release notes. No plugin behaviour changes.

Maintenance release. The manifest changelog field and the letterboxdsync.dev Releases page now match the v1.0–v1.12 single-paragraph user-facing prose style after v1.13.0 (rendered as a multi-paragraph incident report) and v1.13.1 (rendered as the raw conventional-commit subject line) drifted away from it. The release workflow now pulls the manifest changelog from a `## Release notes` section in the merged PR's body via the GitHub API, so the prose that lands in users' plugin catalogs is deliberate and reviewable. Backfills the two missing structured entries on the Releases page and rewrites the two stale manifest entries inline. No plugin behaviour changes.

Maintenance release: stronger release pipeline. Every PR now bumps the version (gated by a required CI check) and auto-ships on merge to main, PR titles must follow Conventional Commits, and letterboxdsync.dev rebuilds on every release. No plugin behaviour changes. Past incident behind this work: v1.13.0 was cut manually after merge and the site Releases page was stale through both v1.12.0 and v1.13.0 because the manifest auto-commit could not trigger Deploy site.

Required update for Jellyfin 10.11.9 and newer. Jellyfin 10.11.9 removed the Users property from IUserManager and replaced it with a GetUsers() method, so the plugin (compiled against the 10.11.0 SDK) threw MissingMethodException on every user-list read on 10.11.9 and 10.11.10. Symptoms before this fix: the dashboard Stats and History endpoints returned 500, the Sync watched movies to Letterboxd scheduled task failed immediately, and Sync Letterboxd watchlist to playlist failed the same way. Plugin behaviour is otherwise unchanged from v1.12.0. targetAbi is now 10.11.9.0, so Jellyfin 10.11.0 through 10.11.8 servers stay on v1.12.0 via the catalog gate; upgrade Jellyfin to 10.11.9 or newer to receive future plugin updates. Fixes #46.

Multi-account support: one Jellyfin user can now link multiple Letterboxd accounts. Auto-sync (real-time on playback completion and scheduled) fans out across every enabled account, with per-account failures isolated. Manual /Sync, /SyncWatchlist, and /Review endpoints accept an optional letterboxdUsername selector and fan out by default when omitted. Diary import unions played-state across all accounts and merges ratings with the primary account winning conflicts (existing Jellyfin ratings are still preserved). Watchlist playlists are now per-account (default name: 'Letterboxd Watchlist ({letterboxdUsername})', overridable per account). New IsPrimary flag on each account, normalised on save (at most one primary per Jellyfin user). UI: the sidebar 'My Letterboxd' page now has feature parity with the admin page for per-account management (add, remove, test, configure every account belonging to your Jellyfin user without admin access). Review modal exposes a 'Post as' account selector when more than one account is enabled, defaulting to all accounts. Behaviour change: existing single-account users will see a new per-account watchlist playlist created on first sync after upgrade, the old 'Letterboxd Watchlist' playlist is left untouched.

Docs: when a Cloudflare 403 happens after you've already pasted Raw Cookies and a matching User-Agent, the plugin error message and README now explain why (cf_clearance is short-lived, pinned to the IP that solved the challenge, and the connection itself is TLS-fingerprinted) and what to try. Addresses the dead-end case reported in #34. No plugin behaviour changes.

Fix: with diary-import enabled, the daily sync was posting phantom rewatch entries to Letterboxd for films you had only marked played via diary import (never actually watched on Jellyfin). The runner now suppresses these films until a real Jellyfin playback sets a LastPlayedDate, at which point the rewatch lands on Letterboxd as expected. Docs: install instructions now call out the File Transformation plugin as a prerequisite for the in-sidebar Letterboxd link.

Fix: watchlisting a TV show on Letterboxd no longer auto-requests an unrelated movie in Jellyseerr. TMDb has independent ID namespaces for movies and TV (e.g. tv/198102 = Hijack, movie/198102 = Cutie Honey Flash), and the link extractor was treating every tmdb link as a movie ID. Now skips links whose URL points at /tv/. Adds regression coverage for the mismatch.

Bidirectional rating sync: dashboard reviews mirror their star rating into Jellyfin's UserItemData.Rating (always overwrites), and the daily diary import seeds Jellyfin ratings from Letterboxd for films that don't yet have a Jellyfin rating (anti-clobber). Switched the diary import API path from /log-entries to /films?memberRelationship=Watched so films you rated on Letterboxd without logging a watch now sync too. New in-dashboard Logs tab with per-user and free-text filters, copy-to-clipboard, and download-as-.log for support requests. Privacy hardening: review text is no longer logged.
Maintenance: bump GitHub Actions runtime versions (checkout v6, setup-dotnet v5, action-gh-release v3) to remain on a supported Node version. No plugin behaviour changes.

Mirror Letterboxd watchlist into Jellyseerr's user watchlist (per-account toggle, two-way sync, movies-only so manually-added Jellyseerr TV is safe). On-demand 'Sync Watchlist Now' button on the plugin dashboard so you don't have to wait for the daily run. Pre-flight check against Jellyseerr's media status eliminates duplicate requests on every run (was creating fresh requests for already-pending/processing/available titles). Per-user watchlist sync runner extracted with a shared SyncGate so diary and watchlist syncs serialise.

Local-history duplicate backstop: refuse to MarkAsWatched when sync history shows a recent successful sync that does not pass the rewatch threshold, fixes the Cloudflare-failed-validator path that was creating real Letterboxd diary duplicates. Paginated dashboard history table (100 per page) now that the 500-entry cap is gone. Addresses #21.

Skip already-synced films using local sync history so we don't burn Cloudflare quota on duplicate checks; prioritise previously-failed/skipped films first; per-account stop-on-failure toggle to halt the moment Letterboxd anti-flooding triggers; explicit info-level logging for every skip with reason; non-admin users can now Run Sync Now (triggers their account only). Fixes #20.
Jellyseerr auto-request for unmatched watchlist films (per-user attribution via Jellyfin User ID), plus dedup fix so the watchlist playlist no longer accumulates duplicate entries on each run
Per-account User-Agent override so Cloudflare cookies copied from any browser (Chrome, Safari, etc.) work without UA mismatch
Fix review posting via official API: resolve film LID from TMDb ID instead of slug (fixes #12)
Official Letterboxd API integration (primary) with web scraping fallback, eliminates Cloudflare 403 errors
User self-service account setup, sidebar link for all users, test connection button, standalone user page via File Transformation injection
Architecture refactor, TMDb cache, progress dashboard, diary import fix, Cloudflare resilience, watchlist cleanup
Real-time playback sync via PlaybackHandler, automatic session re-auth on 401
Fix sync history persistence across version upgrades
Star ratings in reviews, rewatch date picker, Cloudflare retry on reviews, better error display, sync history persistence fix
Dashboard with sync history, watchlist sync, diary import, reviews, Cloudflare backoff, rating sync, rewatch detection
Initial release: real-time sync, scheduled catch-up, multi-user, duplicate detection, retry with backoff

# Release v8.1.0.0

### Umfassendes Update mit neuer Vue.js Web-Oberfläche (Beta) und verbesserten Download-Funktionen.

###  🚀 Neue Funktionen

   * Neue Vue.js WebUI (Beta): Die gesamte Benutzeroberfläche wurde auf Vue.js umgestellt, um eine modernere und flüssigere Bedienung zu ermöglichen.
       * Test-Phase: Dies ist ein erster Test der neuen UI. Sie ist funktional, aber es können noch Fehler auftreten.

###  Dieses Update führt ein völlig neues System zur Pfadverwaltung ein, macht die Suche deutlich mächtiger und verbessert die Benutzererfahrung durch eine direkte Videovorschau.

 ## 🚀 Neue Funktionen
   * Kontextbasiertes Pfad-Management: Anstelle eines einzigen globalen Download-Ordners können nun spezifische Standardpfade für verschiedene Mediathek-Inhalte festgelegt werden:
       * Filme & Serien: Getrennte Basisordner ermöglichen eine saubere, automatische Integration in die jeweilige Jellyfin-Bibliothek.
       * Abonnements & Manuelle Downloads: Eigene Zielverzeichnisse sorgen für eine bessere Organisation Ihrer Medien.
   * Direkte Videovorschau (Play-Button): Suchergebnisse verfügen nun über einen Play-Button. Damit lassen sich die MP4-Direktlinks der Sender sofort im Browser öffnen, um Inhalte vor dem Download kurz zu sichten.
   * Intelligente Sucherweiterung:
       * Kombinierte Abfragen: Die Suche erlaubt nun die gleichzeitige Eingabe von Titel und Thema, um Treffer in großen Mediatheken (z.B. ARD/ZDF) präziser einzugrenzen.
       * Auto-Pre-Fill: Der Dialog für erweiterte Downloads wird jetzt automatisch mit erkannten Metadaten und Pfadvorschlägen (basierend auf der Videoanalyse) vorausgefüllt.
       * Optimierte Eingabe: Suchfelder wachsen nun dynamisch mit dem Text mit (auto-grow).
   * UI-Verbesserungen: Die Standard-Pfadeinstellungen in der Konfiguration sind jetzt einklappbar, um die Übersichtlichkeit zu erhöhen.

 ## 🛠️ Verbesserungen & Refactoring
   * Restrukturierung der Web-UI: Komplette Trennung von HTML-Struktur und JavaScript-Logik zur Verbesserung der Wartbarkeit und Ladezeiten.
   * Robuste Verzeichniserstellung: Die Logik zur automatischen Erstellung von Jellyfin-konformen Ordnerstrukturen wurde grundlegend verbessert.
   * Metadaten-Logik: Verfeinerte Integration von DuckDuckGo und TMDB-Suchen für eine bessere Zuordnung von Postern und Beschreibungen.

 ## 🐞 Bugfixes
   * Sicherheits-Update: Implementierung eines Schutzes gegen Path-Traversal-Angriffe bei der manuellen Pfadeingabe für Downloads.
   * Stabilität: Behebung von Fehlern in den Unit-Tests, die durch die Umstellung auf das neue Pfad-Schema entstanden waren.

# Release v0.6.1.0

This minor release introduces several usability improvements, optimizations for library scanning, and fixes for download management.

   * Plugin Settings in Sidebar: The plugin settings page is now directly accessible from the left sidebar in the Jellyfin Admin Dashboard for easier access #57

   * Optimized Library Scanning: Library scans are now smarter; the plugin waits until all queued downloads in a batch are finished before triggering a scan, preventing redundant scans and reducing system load  #54 

## 🐛 Bug Fixes

   * Prevent Duplicate Downloads: Fixed an issue where existing videos were sometimes re-added to the download list. The logic for checking existing files and quality upgrades has been refactored and made more robust using a new
     FileType system #56 
## 🔧 Internal

   * Refactored File Handling: Introduced a FileType enum to explicitly manage media types (Video, Audio, Strm, Subtitle), improving internal logic for file naming and path generation.
   * Build: Enabled deterministic builds for reproducible release artifacts.

  This release brings significant improvements to subscription management, file maintenance, and the underlying architecture of the plugin.

 ### 🚀 New Features

   * Automated `.strm` Cleanup: A new scheduled task scans your download directories for invalid .strm files. It safely deletes files only if the stream URL is definitively gone (404/410), keeping your library clean without
     risking accidental deletions during server outages.
   * Subscription Management: You can now enable or disable individual subscriptions without deleting them.
   * Smart Duplicate Detection: The plugin now scans the target directory for existing episodes (SxxExx or absolute numbering) to prevent redundant downloads.
   * Library Scan Toggle: Added an option to choose whether the Jellyfin library should be scanned automatically after a download finishes.
   * Enhanced Extras Handling: Better detection and handling of non-episode content (Trailers, Interviews) with options to save them as separate .strm files.

 ### 🐛 Bug Fixes & Improvements

   * Language Detection: Fixed an issue where short words in titles were misinterpret as language codes.
   * API Stability: Fixed API response mapping (replaced missing Total field with QueryInfo).

 ### 🛠 Technical Improvements

   * Major Refactoring: The download logic has been split into SubscriptionProcessor and DownloadManager for better stability and maintainability.
   * Frontend Modernization: Refactored the configuration page to use ES6 classes and safer DOM manipulation.
   * Grouped Downloads: Video and subtitle downloads are now grouped into a single logical job.

Hotfix for 1.0.7.6 Playability false-positives.

• Removed the bitrate-vs-size pre-filter that flagged efficient x264 rips (YIFY / small MP4 rips of Severance / Landman / Rage / Outlander at 400 MB–2.4 GB) as size-truncated. Decode-check already catches genuine tail-truncation with far fewer false positives.

• DRM detection: encrypted MP4/M4V/M4A/MOV (Fairplay / Widevine / PlayReady) detected via codec_tag_string=encv/enca and skipped instead of mis-flagged.

• Folder-based library items (BDMV / VIDEO_TS / mounted-ISO / BDRemux) no longer reported as missing files.

Anyone on 1.0.7.6 should update — the 1.0.7.6 repair ladder would try to salvage these false positives and recycle files that failed repair.

1.0.7.4 is a small follow-up to 1.0.7.3's combined audio + subtitle cleanup pass, closing the last case where MediaDash could ffmpeg the same file twice in one fix run.

When a file had a queued re-encode AND queued track cleanup (unwanted audio or subtitle languages), it used to remux for the tracks first and then re-encode a second time. The re-encode already drops unwanted tracks by itself, so the first remux was wasted work — and if it didn't run first, it would fail with "nothing to remove" once the re-encode had finished. Now the fix run detects the overlap and lets the re-encode handle both jobs in one pass. Same recycle bin entry, one history row per issue, both track and quality issues flip to Fixed together.

User-visible impact: multi-language 4K remuxes that also need size reduction finish in half the time, and the Errors tab stops picking up spurious "nothing to remove" failures on files that were just re-encoded.

1.0.7.3 addresses the loudest bug reports from GitHub issues and the r/jellyfin + r/JellyfinCommunity threads.

Recycle bin: overhauled with rich per-row metadata (BinPath, Provenance, Reason, IssueType, ActionText, RestoreHint, auto-purge countdown), origin-manifest sidecars so restores survive history loss, cross-volume consolidation of legacy bin locations, non-destructive restore that suffixes -restored instead of overwriting, and a 3 GB / 5 GB free-space floor that pauses fix runs and refuses config save on a full bin volume. New endpoints: /RecycleBin/OtherBins, /RecycleBin/Consolidate, /RecycleBin/DiskInfo.

Duplicate detection: keys now include ProductionYear so remakes stop collapsing (#3), keeper picker excludes symlinks and 0-byte files (F-098), DuplicateMinAgeDays default 7 to 0 with one INFO line naming vetoed count.

Fixer output: TrackFixer + TranscodeFixer restore source CreationTimeUtc and LastWriteTimeUtc so Recently-Added stays honest (#31); dry-run stale-failure path no longer flips vanished files to Fixed; per-sidecar history fan-out via FixResult.AdditionalRecycled gives every recycled sidecar its own Restore button; subtitle-provider quota mid-run is now detected and handled quietly.

Playability: cross-checks ffprobe format_name against extension so an MKV renamed .mp3 emits container-extension-mismatch (F-213). HasTruncationMarker no longer treats the benign Truncating packet warning as truncation - that warning fires on real-world MKV cluster boundaries, MPEG-TS packet alignment, and MP4 mdat overlap on files that play fine in Jellyfin (Reddit reports: friskyapple, oogoom, moonplaza, Commercial-Camp-8052). Only File ended prematurely now counts.

TrackFixer ffmpeg command gains -fflags +genpts at input and -avoid_negative_ts make_zero at output - fixes the mpegts sample rate not set / Could not write header failure on Blu-ray-derived .m2ts sources, and lets OutputVerifier accept legitimate long-form duration drift (#39, slack widened from fixed 2 s to max(2 s, dur x 2 percent)).

Combined ffmpeg pass (#28, #32): FixTask now detects same-file AudioLanguage + SubtitleLanguage pairs before the fix loop and routes them through a new TrackFixer.FixCombinedAsync so one ffmpeg drops both categories in a single pass instead of two back-to-back remuxes. Two history rows recorded, one bin entry, both issues flip to Fixed.

SMART noise dedup: SmartHealthProbeWmi caches per-drive-letter WMI failures and SmartHealthProbe caches per-device smartctl timeout / IO / non-zero-exit failures. First failure per device per session still emits the diagnostic; subsequent failures on the same device are suppressed until restart. Addresses the Errors-tab spam on NVMe + mount-point setups (#38, #23).

Files: new read-only Jellyfin logs shortcut at the file-browser root supporting listing + per-file download so users can attach logs to bug reports; ApiKey= param renamed from api_key= for Jellyfin 10.10+ compatibility.

Diagnostics: Copy diagnostics button relabelled Report an issue (copies diagnostics + opens issue tracker in a new tab).

Reliability hotfix: fixes the "13 files locked, nothing holding them" report class by switching every scanner/probe (ArtworkScanner, NfoScanner, TrickplayOptimizeScanner, BookProbeService, FileHasher) from File.OpenRead (default FileShare.Read blocks concurrent moves/deletes on Windows and shows up as ERROR_SHARING_VIOLATION 32) to a new MediaFileHelper.OpenSharedRead helper using FileShare.ReadWrite | Delete. Also splits FixTask's catch-all "disk error" into four accurate diagnostic keys — FixTask.FileMissing (marks issue Fixed so retry stops), FixTask.FileLocked (sharing violation post-retry), FixTask.DiskFull (real ENOSPC only, HResult 112/39/28), residual FixTask.IOError; every bucket gets a new Errors-tab entry with actionable copy. Adds a 5s per-library-root probe to ScanTask so a hard-mounted dead NFS/SMB share can't hang the ThreadPool and force LXC restarts — unreachable roots are skipped with a diagnostic pointing at soft,timeo=30,retrans=3 mount flags. Cleans up Ffmpeg.Timeout noise on Blu-ray remuxes: TrackFixer's 30-min first pass no longer surfaces to Errors (only the 5-hour retry's failure does), Track.RemuxRetry diagnostic removed as it fired on the happy path. New README Uninstall section explaining the remove-repo -> uninstall -> restart sequence so Jellyfin's Update Plugins task can't race the deleteOnStartup marker. Still one binary for both Jellyfin 10.11 and 12.0.

Duplicate detection rework with a per-pair confidence ladder (Exact 1.00 / Identified 0.90 / Heuristic 0.70) plus two hard vetoes (title-token Jaccard, runtime delta) that kill the GitHub #3 Futurama-specials false-positive class.

Fixes
- GitHub #3 - duplicate false positives on distinct files sharing an episode metadata slot.
- GitHub #12 - container CPU/RAM cards showed HOST numbers; now read cgroup v2 -> v1 first and fall through to /proc only when unbounded.
- GitHub #6 + #12-SMART - Linux SMART reported Unknown forever on drives whose libraries live on a partition; now walks partition -> disk via lsblk.
- ArtworkFixer clears the item's ImageInfos BEFORE deleting the file on disk so /Items/{id}/Images/Primary stops 404-ing after a corrupt-artwork sweep.
- Dry-run is now airtight: MissingSubtitleFixer no longer queries external subtitle providers under dry-run (was leaking which files exist and burning provider quota).
- Field report A1: default-threaded ffmpeg pinned every core on a 1-2 vCPU Docker VM and locked up SSH. Threads default to max(1, ProcessorCount/2).
- Field reports A9/A10: reworded 'original kept in recycle bin' and dry-run preview action text so users stop reading it as 'MediaDash is hoarding files'.
- Field report B1: sidecars now follow the primary file after a successful move.
- Field report B4: subtitles in Subtitles/ or Subs/ subfolders next to media are detected.
- Field report D2: MissingSubtitle now runs before Transcode so subtitles land before an encode that would rename-orphan them.
- NfoScanner no longer flags valid metadata as corrupt on missing per-Actor extensions or trailing text after </movie>.
- OrphanCleanupScanner: unrelated adjacent folders no longer treated as orphans; scanners emitting non-video paths opt out of scoped-delete so stale rows don't sit forever.
- EmbeddedCoverArtScanner: no longer flags every non-trivial AVI as corrupt.
- SmartHealth probe: no longer stuck on 'Checking SMART status...' forever on probe crash; PowerShell reliability-counter fallback no longer silently misses on trailing whitespace in FriendlyName.
- RecycleBin cross-volume move: .mediadash.tmp staging file is cleaned up when a move throws mid-way.
- LibraryMonitor: ReportFileSystemChanged now fires for both source and destination on move so cached ImageInfo drops.

Privacy
- Anonymous community-stats install ID is now month-rotated: SHA-256(salt || Jellyfin SystemId || year-month), never stored on disk. Prior persistent UUID was stronger linkability than APP/GDPR tolerates for 'aggregate community stats'.

Duplicates - new config
- DuplicateAutoFixConfidence (default 0.80): under Automatic mode, only pairs at or above this confidence are auto-queued.
- DuplicateTitleJaccardVeto (default 0.40): kills pairs whose filename title tokens overlap less than this.
- DuplicateRuntimeVetoPct (default 15%): kills pairs whose runtimes differ by more than this.
- New file_hashes cache table and Confidence column on issues (idempotent migration to schema v4).

Still one binary for both Jellyfin 10.11 and 12.0.

Features

Reclaim totals now match across the plugin, heavy-transcode fixer works on well-encoded sources, SMART shows correctly on unprivileged Linux, and the History tab lets you slice failures by reason.

Features
- History tab's Failed filter now surfaces a "search by reason" dropdown listing the distinct failure reasons in your history with a count each (Permission denied, I/O error, Cross-device link, File no longer exists, etc.). Selecting one narrows the list; switching the top-level chip clears it.
- SMART pill on the Overview drives now shows a specific hint when smartctl fails due to permissions on Linux: setcap 'cap_sys_rawio+ep' $(which smartctl) for native installs, --cap-add=SYS_RAWIO --device=... for Docker.

Bug fixes
- Overview "Reclaimed since install" and History tab's summary + per-library chart now show the same number. History was summing the paginated 500-row window client-side while Overview summed the entire history server-side, causing the mismatch (e.g. 599 GB vs 8.1 GB). New /History/Stats endpoint aggregates over all history server-side; both panels source the total from it.
- Heavy-transcode / failed-transcode fixes no longer refuse to swap when the re-encoded file is slightly larger than the original. Those fix types exist for direct-play compatibility, not disk savings â€” the size gate is now Quality-only, with a 30% hard cap on the transcode types to guard against misconfigured encode settings.
- SMART pills now appear on library drives on Linux. Library-drive detection was using Path.GetPathRoot which always returns "/" on Linux â€” no library drive was ever flagged, so the SMART probe never ran there. Now uses the deepest-matching mount point via FindDriveForPath.
- smartctl exit_status is now honoured. Non-zero exit (permission denied, unsupported device, no SMART support) returns Unknown with the actual smartctl error message, instead of being mis-interpreted as "self-assessment FAILED".

- RecycleBin cross-volume moves verify copy size before deleting the source (no more silent data loss on truncated writes).
- MoveToBin folder names carry a per-batch GUID so same-millisecond recycles no longer collide.
- FileBrowser rename / move now return 409 on concurrent-target creation instead of silently overwriting.

- TrackFixer.IsSelfReferentialSubtitle normalises both paths via Path.GetFullPath so legacy relative-path issue rows can't trick the guard.
- MediaSorterFixer cross-volume detection works on Linux (was previously blind because Path.GetPathRoot returns "/").
- MissingSubtitleFixer catches TaskCanceledException from provider network stalls without aborting the whole fix run.
- smartctl / nvidia-smi / df invocations use ArgumentList (no shell tokenization); absolute-path resolution on Linux where possible.
- WMI drive-letter validated before WQL interpolation.
- BulkUpdateOpenIssueStatus chunks at 500 params; controller caps requests at 50 k IDs.
- SmartHealthProbe stdout and stderr drained concurrently before WaitForExit (no more pipe-buffer deadlocks on large SMART payloads).
- Diagnostics ring buffer dedup keys off a hash of the pre-truncation message; entries are replaced (not mutated) so concurrent Recent() callers can't observe torn reads.
- AssSubtitleFile.Parse caps input at 100 MB to prevent OOM on malformed sidecars.
- Wizard i18n guard relaxed to Math.min so partial locale translations override index-by-index instead of falling back entirely to English.
- Retention slider in Settings now runs to 365 days (matched the wizard, no more silent 90-day cap on save).

- AnalyticsEnabled default flipped to false to match every "off by default" string in the UI.

New Overview banner warns when a MediaDash re-encode gets undone by something external (typically Sonarr/Radarr redownloading a "too-small" file whose size dropped below the quality profile minimum, but also fires on manual recycle-bin restores or backup-restore overwrites).

Detection is evidence-based, not guessed: at the end of every scan MediaDash walks the last 30 days of successful non-dry-run history entries, and for each one where the ORIGINAL is still preserved in the recycle bin, compares the file currently at the same path against the recycled original. If the current file is within 10% of the original size â€” i.e. the same rough size we shrank down â€” the shrunk copy has been replaced. Only paths meeting that concrete size-match trigger the warning. False positives are limited to genuine restores, which are also worth surfacing.

The red banner shows the filename, the shrunk-to size, the current size, and the fix date. Dismissable per browser session; reappears on the next scan if the condition still holds.

Two fixes and a reclaim.

VAAPI hardware encodes now pass -rc_mode VBR to hevc_vaapi / h264_vaapi / av1_vaapi. Mesa VAAPI's default rate-control is CQP, which ignores -b:v/-maxrate and picks a QP that routinely produces output LARGER than a modest-bitrate source â€” the "the re-encoded file would be larger than the original, so the original was kept" retry loop that some AMD iGPU users saw every 30-70 minutes on the same file. VBR honours -b:v as the target and -maxrate as the ceiling, so the encoder actually stays under the requested bitrate.

Orphan sidecar sweep: at the end of every fix run (right after the recycle bin purge), MediaDash now walks each library root and deletes any *.mediadash.tmp*, *.mediadash.new*, mediadash.tmp.*, or mediadash.new.* file it finds. These are leftovers from a hard-killed encode (SIGKILL, container restart, Jellyfin crash) where the C# finally block that normally deletes them never ran. Deleted-count + reclaimed-bytes go into Jellyfin's log.

Orphan sidecar sweep: at the end of every fix run (right after the recycle bin purge), MediaDash now walks each library root and deletes any *.mediadash.tmp*, *.mediadash.new*, mediadash.tmp.*, or mediadash.new.* file it finds. These are leftovers from a hard-killed encode (SIGKILL, container restart, Jellyfin crash) where the C# finally block that normally deletes them never ran. Deleted-count + reclaimed-bytes go into Jellyfin's log.

FfmpegExecutor now sweeps for orphaned MediaDash ffmpeg processes before spawning a new encode. Linux only (reads /proc/<pid>/cmdline; Windows/macOS would need extra deps for a very rare failure mode). Any ffmpeg whose command line contains a mediadash.tmp or mediadash.new marker is killed with SIGKILL and its sidecar output file is deleted. Prevents the "two ffmpegs writing to the same output" scenario after a plugin hot-reload or a Jellyfin restart mid-encode. Also cleans up the interleaved-bytes .tmp file that would otherwise sit on disk until the next fix run on the same source overwrote it.

versions.changelog: Consider artist id when syncing favourites
Fix for tracks without album artist metadata.
Fixed audiobooks being incorrectly treated as music and sent to Last.fm as now playing tracks, scrobbles, or favourite updates.

Scrobble log messages now include the exact data sent to Last.fm, url encoded and without the credentials, so a rejected scrobble can be replayed as is. This also covers the album artist and the MusicBrainz id, which were never logged before, and makes characters that are invisible in a log, such as non breaking spaces in artist names, easy to spot. This only changes logging, scrobbling behaviour is unchanged.

Playback events received from Jellyfin are now logged, in both the default and the alternative mode, to help debug reports of tracks that never get scrobbled. Some clients do not tell the server that a track was played or stopped, and until now there was no way to tell that apart from the plugin discarding the event. The reason a track was skipped is logged as well. This only adds logging, scrobbling behaviour is unchanged.

Scrobbles that Last.fm silently drops are now logged as warnings with the reason, instead of being reported as successful. Last.fm answers those with a normal HTTP 200 and no error code, so they were previously indistinguishable from accepted scrobbles in the logs. This does not change which scrobbles are accepted, it only makes the rejected ones visible.

This version requires Jellyfin 10.11.9 or newer. Jellyfin 10.11.9 changed an internal API the plugin relies on. Fixes the 'Import Last.fm Loved Tracks' task. Also refactored the settings page to use plugin-specific element IDs, avoiding clashes with other plugins' configuration pages - this might fix the user dropdown showing up empty for some users.

New API key and secret, since the previous one was blocked or deleted by the original project owner. After upgrading, every user will need to re-enter their credentials for the plugin to work again. There's no way to migrate the old credentials since the API key is different and we don't store the actual user password (we just use it to create a session key). This is a necessary change to keep the plugin working, since the stored session keys were generated with the previous API key that is not valid anymore.

name: Marquee Companion [✓]
description:
Adds four independent capabilities: server-side filtering by media-stream characteristics that Jellyfin's core API can't express (video dynamic range, codecs, audio channel count, and spatial audio), plus opt-in global recent-podcast discovery via Podcast Index using administrator-provided credentials, plus opt-in passwordless sign-in by emailed magic link over administrator-configured SMTP, plus an opt-in scheduled task that recovers the release date of items that arrived without one by reading it from the file name. The filtering API exposes a paginated, BaseItemDto-compatible endpoint and a capability endpoint for client feature-detection.

versions.changelog:
- Initial release. - Resolution (isHd/is4K) passthrough for client filtering. - Fix: filtering by a library returned no items. The library (parentId) is now
  resolved into its contents so video range / codec / audio filters work when
  scoped to a specific library.
- Renamed the plugin to "Marquee Companion" (display name only; API route,
  plugin id, and behavior unchanged).
- Capabilities are now scoped to the requested library (parentId): the available
  values offered for a library are drawn only from items in that library, so any
  single facet selection is guaranteed to match at least one item there. Omitting
  parentId still returns the global value set.
- TV libraries now filter correctly by stream facets. Stream attributes live on
  episodes, but TV libraries are browsed at the series level; the filter now
  matches episodes and returns the shows that have at least one matching episode.
  Also forces a recursive query so a library id resolves to its contents.
- Added opt-in recent podcast discovery through Podcast Index. - Podcast discovery now logs why it returned nothing. The endpoint still answers 404 for
  every failure, but the server log distinguishes disabled credentials, a Podcast Index
  rejection, and feeds dropped during validation — including a per-rule tally of what was
  dropped.
- Removes the YouTube trailer resolver. Clients now hand YouTube trailers to the YouTube
  app instead, so the server no longer downloads, verifies, updates, or executes yt-dlp or a
  JavaScript runtime.
- Removes the yt-dlp and JavaScript-runtime downloads earlier versions installed. Those
  binaries are unreachable now the resolver is gone, so the plugin reclaims the directory it
  created rather than leaving an administrator to find it. Only its own install root is
  touched, and a failure to delete never stops the plugin starting.

  failed to deserialize. Both the boolean and the documented string form are now accepted, and
  an unusable payload is logged with the value exactly as it arrived.

  link, and confirming that link signs the waiting device in — no password, and no typing on a
  TV remote. The email can be opened on any device, so it works for tvOS; when it is opened on
  the signing-in device itself, the confirmation page also offers a deep link straight back into
  the app. Unrecognised addresses can optionally register, in which case the new account is
  created disabled and copies an administrator-chosen template user's permissions, so nothing is
  accessible until an administrator enables it. SMTP host, port, security, credentials and
  from-address are configured in the plugin settings, along with link lifetime and rate limits;

  endpoint reports an explicit error rather than a silent success when SMTP is not configured.

  date only in the file name, so Jellyfin stores no premiere date and reads the leading

  TV remote. The email can be opened on any device, so it works for tvOS; when it is opened on
  the signing-in device itself, the confirmation page also offers a deep link straight back into
  the app. Unrecognised addresses can optionally register, in which case the new account is
  created disabled and copies an administrator-chosen template user's permissions, so nothing is
  accessible until an administrator enables it. SMTP host, port, security, credentials and
  from-address are configured in the plugin settings, along with link lifetime and rate limits;
  a "send test email" button reports the mail server's own error when submission fails. The
  endpoint reports an explicit error rather than a silent success when SMTP is not configured.
- Fix: an audio filter matched files that had each thing you asked for, but never in
  the same track. Asking for AC-3 in 5.1 returned 444 movies on a test library, of which
  only 247 had an AC-3 track that was itself 5.1 — the rest were "DTS 5.1 main track plus
  AC-3 2.0 commentary" files that answered "has AC-3" and "has six channels" separately.
  Codec, channel count and spatial format are now read per audio track and have to hold on
  ONE of them. A filter naming a single audio facet is unaffected. The values offered by
  /Capabilities are unchanged.
- Music libraries can now be filtered by codec and channel count. Tracks were never
  catalogued, so every audio filter over a music library returned nothing at all while the
  same library unfiltered returned 11,022 tracks.
- Release-date recovery reads the FILE NAME first and falls back to date added, and
  understands two-digit-year release names (Name.25.02.05.Title). Date added is when a
  file reached the server, not when it was released: on a 650-item dry run, leading with
  it produced 18 distinct dates with 605 identical, while the name gave 98 spanning 2013
  to 2026.
- Release-date recovery is chosen PER LIBRARY. - Added opt-in release-date recovery. Downloaded YouTube content carries its upload
  date only in the file name, so Jellyfin stores no premiere date and reads the leading
  YYYYMMDD as a production year like 20250823 — those items then cannot appear in any
  view ordered by release date, on any client. A new scheduled task, "Recover missing
  release dates", reads the date from the production-year stamp, an sYYYY.eMMDDnn name,
  or a bare YYYYMMDD run, and writes it along with the corrected year. Off by default,
  previews to the log until an administrator turns preview off, and never modifies an
  item that already has a release date.
- Adds the seamless Marquee Companion panel to Jellyfin Web without manual web-client changes. - Adds paired Jellyfin 10/.NET 9 and Jellyfin 12/.NET 10 package builds.

- Initial release. - Resolution (isHd/is4K) passthrough for client filtering. - Fix: filtering by a library returned no items. The library (parentId) is now
  resolved into its contents so video range / codec / audio filters work when
  scoped to a specific library.
- Renamed the plugin to "Marquee Companion" (display name only; API route,
  plugin id, and behavior unchanged).
- Capabilities are now scoped to the requested library (parentId): the available
  values offered for a library are drawn only from items in that library, so any
  single facet selection is guaranteed to match at least one item there. Omitting
  parentId still returns the global value set.
- TV libraries now filter correctly by stream facets. Stream attributes live on
  episodes, but TV libraries are browsed at the series level; the filter now
  matches episodes and returns the shows that have at least one matching episode.
  Also forces a recursive query so a library id resolves to its contents.
- Added opt-in recent podcast discovery through Podcast Index. - Podcast discovery now logs why it returned nothing. The endpoint still answers 404 for
  every failure, but the server log distinguishes disabled credentials, a Podcast Index
  rejection, and feeds dropped during validation — including a per-rule tally of what was
  dropped.
- Removes the YouTube trailer resolver. Clients now hand YouTube trailers to the YouTube
  app instead, so the server no longer downloads, verifies, updates, or executes yt-dlp or a
  JavaScript runtime.
- Removes the yt-dlp and JavaScript-runtime downloads earlier versions installed. Those
  binaries are unreachable now the resolver is gone, so the plugin reclaims the directory it
  created rather than leaving an administrator to find it. Only its own install root is
  touched, and a failure to delete never stops the plugin starting.

  `status` as a JSON boolean, but it was bound to a string, so the whole recent-feeds payload
  failed to deserialize. Both the boolean and the documented string form are now accepted, and
  an unusable payload is logged with the value exactly as it arrived.

  degraded. The resolve timeout moves from 10 to 30 seconds to accommodate runtime start-up

description:
Skip sponsored segments in YouTube videos using SponsorBlock data.  
  
Universal Repo:

versions.changelog: Add an opt-in Jellyfin metadata source for YouTube IDs. Preserve filename and custom-regex matching as the default, read validated Youtube provider IDs imported from NFO uniqueid metadata, and expose the source choice in plugin settings.

Add Jellyfin 12 support. Retarget to .NET 10 and Jellyfin Controller 12.0.0-rc3, implement the new media-segment cleanup contract, and preserve the event-driven SponsorBlock workflow without enabling the core library segment scan.
Serialize SponsorBlock processing to avoid concurrent refresh and playback work for the same item. Bump the plugin version for local installation.

Add Done state with convergence-based polling. Videos older than 30 days (by YouTube publish date) are fetched once and frozen. Videos younger than 30 days are polled daily until segment data is unchanged for 5 consecutive checks, then frozen. Stale segments are now deleted when SponsorBlock data disappears. Daily scan task refactored to a clean two-phase dispatcher.

Add dedicated SponsorBlock log file (log_SponsorBlock_YYYYMMDD.log) in Jellyfin's log directory. All info/warning/error events now write to both the main server log and the dedicated file, so the plugin appears as a separate log entry in the Jellyfin dashboard.

Add comprehensive logging to the orchestrator and triggers. Every decision point (scope check, path empty, ID extraction failure, state-machine skip, segment write, state transition) now logs at information or debug level, so issues are diagnosable directly from the Jellyfin log dashboard.
Fix EnumerateScoped to discover Episode and Movie items, not just standalone Video. YouTube libraries imported as TV Shows store items as Episode type, which BaseItemKind.Video did not match.

Fix automatic loading for old archives and restore DLL-only release packaging. The daily refresh now discovers selected-library videos older than the sanity-check window, old untracked items use their Jellyfin DateCreated for the 48-hour decision, and NoData rows recheck after cooldown instead of being terminal.

Add a one-shot Force Scan button for existing archives. Admins can backfill every video in the selected libraries once, while the normal daily refresh stays limited to tracked Pending and HasData items. Includes duplicate-scan protection and status endpoints.

Repair pruned SponsorBlock segments on playback. When Jellyfin refreshes a changed media file it can delete generated MediaSegment rows while the plugin state still says HasData; playback start now verifies that Jellyfin still has segment rows and re-fetches/recreates them if they were pruned.

Fix delayed SponsorBlock loading. Register the daily refresh scheduled task so Pending items are retried automatically, correct the 24-hour playback retry condition, and wait for playback-start processing so freshly fetched segments can reach the first playback session.

Actually fix segments not reaching clients. Jellyfin's IMediaSegmentManager.CreateSegmentAsync expects the second arg to be the MD5-derived provider id (new Guid(MD5(name.ToLowerInvariant() UTF-16 LE)).ToString("N")), not the literal provider name. We were passing "SponsorBlock" verbatim, so stored segments didn't match any registered provider and the public MediaSegments API filtered them out. Pre-compute the hash and pass that. After upgrading, hit Reset on the config page so old segments get re-fetched under the correct provider id.

Fix segments not reaching clients. v1.1.0.0 dropped the IMediaSegmentProvider registration to avoid the slow scan, but Jellyfin filters segments by registered provider, so stored segments were never served. Re-register a stub provider (Supports => false, GetMediaSegments => empty) so Jellyfin recognizes 'SponsorBlock' as a known provider while the orchestrator stays in charge of fetching.

Add admin Reset button on the plugin config page that wipes SponsorBlock state and owned segments for items in the configured library scope, so the orchestrator re-fetches on next playback. Useful for re-fetching items whose SponsorBlock data became available after the initial scan.

Replace media-segment scan with event-driven orchestrator. Add daily refresh task at configurable hour. Add per-library scoping (empty by default — admin must opt in). SQLite per-item state machine (Pending/HasData/NoData) with 48h sanity check.
Remove non-functional user segment actions table from config page.
Initial release.

name: ShareLinks
description:
Adds secure, expiring guest-share links for Jellyfin items using temporary hidden users, one-use token redemption, restrictive policies, and scheduled cleanup.  
  
Universal Repo:  
Generated: 16:08 UTC  
Source: https://raw.githubusercontent.com/Franciskid/jellyfin-plugin-sharelinks/main/manifest.json  
Github: https://github.com/Franciskid/jellyfin-plugin-sharelinks
overview: Temporary guest links for Jellyfin movies and episodes.

versions.changelog: Fixes share links on Jellyfin 12 and the ShareLink button missing on new Docker installs.

Fixes redemption on Jellyfin 10.11.9 and later (#19). Jellyfin changed the signature of the method the plugin uses to set a guest's password, so every link failed with a MissingMethodException and the guest landed on the dead-link page. The plugin now picks whichever version of that method the server has, so the same build works on every 10.11 release. Tested on 10.11.8 and 10.11.11.

Guests are now blocked from other plugins' API endpoints on the server, not just hidden from their UI in the browser. A share guest holds a real Jellyfin token, so anything that only hid a button left the endpoint answering it. Jellyfin's own API is untouched: the share tag already limits it to the shared title, and playback needs it. The config page lists your installed plugins with a checkbox each, so you can let one through when it genuinely needs to serve guests, such as an intro skipper. The guest hidden selectors setting is renamed to say what it is: cosmetic, it tidies the view and enforces nothing. Also fixes the dashboard devices page coming up empty after a share expired: deleting a guest left its device row behind, and a device whose user is missing makes Jellyfin fail the whole device listing rather than skip one row.

Fixes a season share exposing the rest of the series: the tag was going onto the season's parent series, and Jellyfin treats a parent's tags as belonging to all of its children, so every other season became visible to the guest. Tagging now only ever goes downwards. Take this update if you have shared a season with a link that is still live. Also in this release: a link can be made multi-use from the create popup so several people can use it until it expires, with a configurable ceiling on how many watch at once (ten by default), and the dashboard gains a "Clean up finished links" button that removes revoked, expired and failed records.

The ShareLink button now sits in its own section at the bottom of the item menu, and only appears for a movie, series, season or episode instead of turning up on things like a cast member. It is properly admin only again: the current user was cached for the whole page, so switching accounts in the same tab could leave the button visible to a normal user (the server always refused them). Share tags are hidden from everyone except admins, on the title and in the tag filter. Security: one-use links can no longer be redeemed twice, the configured maximum expiry is respected, the raw token is dropped from storage when a link dies, the token secret file is 0600, guest accounts can no longer sign in from the login page at all, and the runtime reflection shims around Jellyfin's APIs are gone.

Series and seasons can now be shared, not just single movies and episodes: the share tags the whole tree so the guest can browse and play everything inside it, and cleanup strips it all again. Expired or invalid links now show a friendly page that redirects to the Jellyfin home instead of raw JSON. The guest hidden selectors setting now defaults to empty.

ShareLink button on the item menu, temporary guest users confined by tag policy, expiring links with a date/time picker, admin dashboard with revoke, and a configurable guest lockdown that hides tag/genre/studio/cast links, the add-to-playlist and add-to-collection actions, and other plugins' UI. The creation popup is localized in English and French. Guest sessions are now minted server side: no password is ever stored or sent anywhere, the guest page only carries a session token, and expired guests are cleaned up every 30 minutes.
